faq.description: Answers to common questions about the 2.7 TDV6 engine in the Land Rover Discovery 4. If yours is not covered, our team can help.

faqs.q: How do you confirm a 276DT engine fits my Discovery 4?
faqs.a: We check your VIN or registration against the engine code, model year, market specification and emissions equipment. TDV6 engines from other models can differ in ancillaries and wiring, so compatibility is confirmed before supply.

faqs.q: How do used, reconditioned and rebuilt 2.7 TDV6 engines compare?
faqs.a: A used engine comes from a donor vehicle, a reconditioned engine is stripped and given new wear parts, and a rebuild restores your existing engine. We recommend an option after assessing the fault and vehicle.

faqs.q: Can I buy a Discovery 4 TDV6 engine supply only?
faqs.a: Yes. Trade buyers, independent garages and private customers with their own mechanic can buy supply only. Alternatively, choose supply and fit and our technicians will install the engine at our Grays, Essex workshop.

faqs.q: What affects the Discovery 4 engine replacement cost for a 276DT?
faqs.a: The cost depends on the engine option, the condition of your current engine, any parts needed such as a turbo or DPF, and the labour involved, including body-off access. Send your registration or VIN for a quote.

faqs.q: Is there a warranty on a replacement 276DT engine?
faqs.a: Warranty cover depends on the engine option and whether we carry out the installation. We confirm the exact terms in writing with your quote, so you know what is covered before work begins.

faqs.q: Do you deliver 2.7 TDV6 engines across the UK?
faqs.a: Yes. We deliver engines throughout the United Kingdom from our Grays workshop. Delivery arrangements and costs are confirmed in your quote, and supply and fit customers can bring their Discovery to us.

faqs.q: How long does a Discovery 4 engine replacement usually take?
faqs.a: The timescale depends on engine availability, whether a rebuild is needed, any body-off work and additional repairs found during inspection. We give you an estimated timeframe with your quote and keep you informed.

workshopIntro.title: Repair, Rebuild or Replace Your Discovery 4 TDV6?
workshopIntro.description: The fault, mileage and value of your Discovery 4 decide the best approach. Injector, turbo, DPF or oil cooler faults can often be repaired individually. If the crankshaft has failed or the bearings are damaged, a rebuild or Land Rover Discovery 4 276DT engine replacement is usually the more sensible long-term choice.
paragraphs: Major engine work on the Discovery 4 can involve separating the body from the chassis, so checking related parts makes sense. Where relevant, we inspect the turbo, oil cooler, intercooler, EGR, DPF and cooling system, and renew the oil, filters and coolant.

Send your registration or VIN with a short description of the symptoms. We will confirm compatibility, explain the options and quote for supply only, supply and fit at our Grays workshop, or delivery across the UK.

engineProblems.title: Common Discovery 4 2.7 TDV6 Faults
engineProblems.description: The 2.7 TDV6 often shows warning signs before serious failure, so early checks help keep costs down.

cards.title: Crankshaft Fracture and Bearing Wear
cards.description: A heavy knock, a low oil pressure warning or a sudden engine stop may indicate bearing wear or a fractured crankshaft on higher-mileage TDV6 engines. We assess the crankshaft, bearings and oil system.

cards.title: Timing Belt Service Neglect
cards.description: The 2.7 TDV6 relies on timing and fuel pump belts. Missed replacement intervals can lead to belt failure and serious valve damage. We check belt condition and service history.

cards.title: Turbo Actuator and Boost Loss
cards.description: Limp mode, flat spots or boost fault codes may come from a sticking variable-vane turbocharger, a failing actuator or a leaking intake hose. We test boost control and turbo condition.
cards.action: Fuel rail and injector leak-off test

cards.title: Oil Cooler Failure
cards.description: Oil in the coolant, coolant in the oil or a milky residue can point to a failed oil cooler or perished internal seals. We check both fluids and pressure-test the system.

cards.title: DPF and Regeneration Problems
cards.description: DPF warnings, frequent regenerations or reduced power often occur when short journeys stop the particulate filter clearing properly. We read live data and assess filter loading.

cards.title: Injector Leaks and Smoke
cards.description: Rough idle, smoke, a fuel smell or poor starting may be caused by leaking injector seals or worn fuel injectors. We test the injectors and inspect the seals.

engineOverview.title: Land Rover Discovery 4 276DT Engine: The Complete 2.7 TDV6 Guide
paragraphs: The Land Rover Discovery 4 276DT engine is the 2.7-litre V6 turbodiesel, known as the 2.7 TDV6, fitted to Discovery 4 models in certain markets before the 3.0 V6 diesel became standard. With mileage, crankshaft failure, timing belt neglect, turbo and DPF problems often lead owners to seek repair or replacement.

The 2.7 TDV6 also appeared in the Discovery 3 and Range Rover Sport, with differences in ancillaries, wiring and emissions equipment. We identify the correct Discovery 4 TDV6 engine by checking your VIN, the engine code and your registration before supply.

Whether you need a targeted repair, an engine rebuild or a complete Discovery 4 276DT engine replacement, our team assesses the vehicle and explains each option. Call us or send your registration for a written quote.
